recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if CDS explicitly decides to add new normative guidance that PlanDefinition action coding should directly use http://hl7.org/fhir/restful-interaction codes; that would be a clarified or new work-group decision beyond this applied R6 text.
issue_request: FHIR-30433 asked how a PlanDefinition action should refer to RESTful interactions such as Patient create or update, instead of inventing implicit Patient/$create or Patient/$update OperationDefinition URLs. The Applied/Persuasive with Modification disposition said the activity inputs and resource body determine the concrete URL and that PlanDefinition/CDS documentation should explain the mechanism.
initial_application: The explicit application is commit bedab38b5ca162114c3b60501fd84a2da9945692, merged in HL7/fhir#3914 for R6. It added a paragraph to source/clinicalreasoning-knowledge-artifact-representation.html explaining that create/update/remove actions realized by PlanDefinition/$apply return proposal resources and that a client application can turn those proposals into RESTful API calls. The immediately preceding FHIR-30209 commit in the same PR added the update-action example qualified by that paragraph.
additional_context: The linked Zulip thread contains the original question about using an implied Patient-create OperationDefinition versus http://hl7.org/fhir/restful-interaction#create. FHIR-I minutes from 2021-01-18 recorded that FHIR-30433 would be documented in PlanDefinition and reassigned to CDS. Current build-scope checks show the Clinical Reasoning page is listed in hierarchy.xml, PlanDefinition is an active CDS resource, and the restful-interaction CodeSystem is active in fhir.ini. The final Jira application comment says this was documented as an application-provided feature because actions can already indicate create/update/delete or use OperationDefinition for operations.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current built source already conveys the applied behavior: PlanDefinition/$apply returns proposals, and the caller may apply create/update/remove proposals by making RESTful API calls. Adding separate URL+code wording now would be redundant and could diverge from the final applied Jira comment.

related_jiras.note: The same PR added the PlanDefinition update-action example immediately before the FHIR-30433 automation paragraph, providing concrete context for create/update/remove behavior. It was not decided here because the seed can be reconciled independently.
